findings.where: script lines 5 and 6 (showError / markError captions and VO)
findings.issue: The same idea is stated twice in a row and in the same two-fragment shape. VO: "One row, one #N/A" then "There's just no row to find." Captions: "New vendor. / No row to find." then "Formula's fine. / The row doesn't exist." Reads like padding and breaks the no-two-captions-with-the-same-shape rule.
findings.fix: Keep one of them. Let the showError beat name the vendor and the markError beat carry a different point (the master just hasn't been updated yet), and change the caption shape so it isn't two fragments again.

findings.issue: The overlay says "LABEL THE MISS YOURSELF" while the voice says "So save it for a lookup you already trust." Two different takeaways land at once, and the sub repeats the spoken line, so the viewer hears the caveat and reads the instruction. Also "the lookup itself is sound" is stiffer than the rest of the script.
findings.fix: Pick one takeaway for the payoff. Either the label line or the caveat, with the sub carrying the other in plainer words ("only on a lookup you already trust").

findings.issue: "or use two empty quote marks if you want the cell blank" overstates slightly. "" leaves an empty text string, not a blank cell, so ISBLANK and COUNTA still see it. Accountants who later count blanks will notice.
findings.fix: Say "if you want it to look blank" or drop the clause; the description already has its search phrase and one sentence.

findings.where: captions at typeFix and the uncued line before it
findings.issue: Three imperative captions run back to back ("Wrap it in IFERROR. / Hand it your own words." then "Spell it out for / the next reader."). Same grammatical shape twice in a row.
findings.fix: Recast the typeFix caption as a statement, e.g. name what the cell will now say instead of telling the viewer to do something again.

findings.issue: Fourth reel built around a VLOOKUP returning #N/A. Wording and hook are genuinely different, so this isn't a template repeat, but the topic cluster is getting heavy.
findings.fix: No change needed here. Pull the next one or two off lookup errors entirely (reconciling a GL export, aging bucket, subtotal drift).

hook.note: "SENT with #N/A down the cost center column" is a real, specific, embarrassing moment (you already sent it) and 8 on-screen words. The lead word "SENT" carries the sting well. Only reason it isn't a 5 is that #N/A on screen is now the fourth time this channel has opened with it.

claims.claim: VLOOKUP with FALSE returns #N/A when the lookup value isn't in the first column of the range
claims.note: Standard exact-match behaviour; matches the verified expected value.

claims.claim: FALSE as the fourth argument means exact match
claims.note: Narration says "exact match" and that's what FALSE/0 does.

claims.claim: Wrapping the lookup in IFERROR substitutes your own text for the error
claims.note: IFERROR returns value_if_error for any error value; verified result is "Not in vendor master".

claims.claim: IFERROR hides a typo or a broken reference just as quietly
claims.note: IFERROR traps all error types, including #NAME? and #REF!, not just #N/A. The caveat is accurate and worth keeping.

claims.claim: Filling down still returns the correct cost center for vendors that are on the master
claims.note: Absolute range $A$8:$B$10 doesn't drift; fillDown values match the master rows.
IFERROR ships in Excel 2007 and later, so a locked-down 2016/2019 install is fine. Correctly silent on versions.

claims.claim: Two empty quote marks make the cell blank
claims.note: Description only. Empty string is not a blank cell for ISBLANK, COUNTA or COUNTBLANK.
